Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 5, Verse 22

“The enjoyments born of contact are only wombs of sorrow, Kaunteya. They have a beginning and an end, and the wise do not take delight in them.”

Wombs of sorrow is a striking phrase — these pleasures do not merely fade, they give birth to the grief that follows. The fault named is precisely their having ends.
